title: Bias Audits Detect Bias but Disagree on Ranking: Evidence from Ten Instruments and Ten Frontier Models
abstract: arXiv:2609.15995v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emerging AI regulation mandates bias audits of high-risk systems, and audit scores are beginning to be used to rank models. Both uses assume different audit tools measure the same thing well enough to compare. We test that assumption directly, running ten extrinsic audit instruments over a shared panel of ten frontier models through one pooled inference gateway, first on occupational gender bias, then on age and socioeconomic status. Detection succeeds while ranking fails. Eight of ten tools detect bias with confidence intervals clear of zero; two widely cited direct-probe benchmarks are saturated because frontier models now answer neutrally. But cross-tool rank agreement is indistinguishable from chance (Kendall's W=0.07, p=0.83). translated_title: 偏见审计能检测偏见但在排名上互不一致：来自十种审计工具与十个前沿模型的证据
translated_abstract: 新兴的人工智能监管要求对高风险系统进行偏见审计，且审计评分开始被用于对模型进行排名。这两种用途都假设不同的审计工具测量的是同一事物，且一致性足以支持模型间的比较。我们直接检验了这一假设：通过一个统一的推理网关，在由十个前沿模型组成的共享模型面板上运行十种外在偏见审计工具，首先针对职业性别偏见，随后针对年龄与社会经济地位偏见。结果显示：检测成功，而排名失败。十个工具中有八个能以置信区间明显偏离零点的方式检测到偏见；两个被广泛引用的直接探测式基准已经饱和，因为前沿模型如今已能给出中性回答。然而，跨工具的排名一致性不优于随机水平（Kendall's W=0.07，p=0.83）。一项以六个刻意较弱模型作为阳性对照的实验区分了两种解释：当模型面板跨越真实的能力差距时，工具内部的可靠性得以恢复，但跨工具的排名始终无法恢复，这一
tldr: 该研究用十种偏见审计工具测试十个前沿模型后发现，尽管偏见检测普遍有效，但不同工具给出的模型排名与随机一致无异（Kendall's W=0.07），表明审计评分尚不可靠于模型排名。
en_tdlr: Testing ten audit instruments on ten frontier models, this study shows that while bias detection succeeds broadly, cross-tool model rankings agree no better than chance (Kendall's W=0.07), indicating audit scores are unreliable for ranking models.
